classification: Realtime delivery-path corrections that return every V2 consumer feed to its freshness policy, plus per-service CPU ceilings, canonical Kafka retention and the Rust runtime rollout that v2.0.15 deferred

delta.defect: Every realtime V2 feed was being served stale or rejected. The stream gateway held one spool lock across a durable read on the live delivery path, so a subscription's delivery rate was bounded by disk; a latest-state feed queued a FIFO of superseded records and could not reach the newest one; a replay token was re-signed on a worker thread per record; and DATA_STALE never said which predicate failed, so the consumer could not tell a slow feed from a dead session. Measured TRADE freshness was 355,952 ms against a 2,000 ms policy and the projector backlog reached 3,002,343 records.

slices.R1.1: the delivery path reads a cached high watermark instead of taking the spool lock for a durable read
slices.R1.2: the replay loop collapses token advances over unmatched runs instead of signing one per record
slices.R1.3: DATA_STALE names its predicate: EVENT_AGE, SESSION_STATE or SESSION_LIVENESS
slices.R1.8: a latest-state feed keeps the newest record in a bounded buffer and drops the superseded ones instead of queueing a FIFO the reader can never drain
slices.R1.9: a cursor whose watermark is already known is signed on the loop instead of paying a thread hop
slices.R1.11: the projector drain window is a configurable budget, not a hard-coded 10 ms constant
slices.R1.12: a subscription that overflows reports backpressure to the consumer instead of discarding records in silence

companion_change.summary: the consumer keeps a valid snapshot view inside its freshness bound instead of tearing the slice down on a retryable DATA_STALE, and bounds a silent subscription

measured_freshness_ms.method: consumer-side benchmark through the real gRPC and HTTP data plane, 8 iterations, 2026-09-17T04:11:44Z, after the offset recovery and on the release image
measured_freshness_ms.receipt: durable event age at the moment each endpoint served it

projector_throughput.method: consumer-group offsets for stable-projector-v1 on md.canonical.v2, 24 snapshots over 356 s at 2026-09-17T04:11:43Z-04:17:39Z
projector_throughput.net: consumed 14 records more than produced; the standing queue drained slightly over the window
projector_throughput.conclusion: there is no backlog; the projector consumes at the rate the ingestors produce

certification_window.method: one sampler per minute reading the projector consumer-group lag and the market_data service heartbeat, two overlapping runs merged by timestamp
certification_window.recovery_lag_gate_bound: 500 total and 250 per partition, instantaneous sample
certification_window.statement: the consumer was not READY on every one of the thirty samples; it was READY on 26, never fell back to V1, and the worst sample had 3 of 60 slices transiently unhealthy

resource_ceilings.method: per-service cpus in docker-compose.v2-stable.yml with the measurement that justified each one; totals summed over the 17 roles this stack actually runs
resource_ceilings.corrects: CERTIFICATION_LEDGER.md entry 24 states 14.35; the resolved sum over the running roles is 13.35
resource_ceilings.raw_retention_reason: raw cannot be refetched; canonical is derived from it

rust_runtime_rollout.status: ALREADY_DEPLOYED, recorded here because v2.0.15 left it as an open boundary
rust_runtime_rollout.closes: the v2.0.15 boundary that left qdl-v2-rust:2.0.12-3f1c50e on rustls 0.23.43

delta.provider_connections: read-only venue REST comparison for the OHLCV check only

python_suite.command: docker run --rm --network none --user $(id -u) -e HOME=/tmp -e PYTHONPATH=/workspace --tmpfs /workspace/logs:mode=1777 --tmpfs /app/logs:mode=1777 -v $PWD:/workspace:ro -w /workspace qdl-v2-python:2.0.16-df4b8aa python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -t .
python_suite.note: network disabled, source mounted read-only, both log directories on tmpfs. Without the /app/logs tmpfs three modules fail to import on a PermissionError writing /app/logs/app.log and discovery reports 1486 tests with errors; that is the environment, not the tests. The v2.0.15 certificate's four pre-existing import errors have the same cause.

boundaries: This patch inherits the v2.0.15 certificate and does not recertify the full product matrix.
Binance MARK_INDEX_PRICE still answers DATA_NOT_READY. It is pre-existing, was not touched by this release, and has its own open slice.
One of sixteen OKX MARK_INDEX_PRICE samples was rejected on EVENT_AGE. The pairing of mark-price with once-per-second index-tickers remains the cause recorded in ledger entry 21.

The 500-total/250-per-partition lag bound is the convergence gate of the projection-cache rebuild runbook (scripts/rebuild_v2_stable_projection_cache.py:31), not a steady-state health gate. At 373 records per second a 500-record bound is 1.3 seconds of work, so an instantaneous sample of a healthy queue crosses it; 5 of 30 window samples did while the consumer stayed ready and never fell back to V1. Steady-state health is the produced-versus-consumed rate and the seconds-of-work figures recorded above. The runbook constant is correct for its own purpose and was deliberately left alone; correcting its use as a health gate is a scheduled slice.
binance_bar_edge stays on qdl-v2-python:2.0.15-5130f6f. It does not use the stream delivery path and was deliberately left on the certified BAR settlement build.

The OKX last closed 1m bar is served about 60 seconds behind the Binance one (96.6 s versus 36.1 s age at measurement). Both are inside the 180 s consumer contract; the difference is the OKX calendar-bar boundary and is not a regression.
The companion consumer change R1.4 lives in the trading_system repository and is not released by this tag.

This release recreated only the seven python roles listed in delta.changed_services. V1, the Kafka topology, Redis, SQLite, binance_bar_edge, the ingestors, the rust cores and alpha were not recreated by it; the rust roles already ran qdl-v2-rust:2.0.15-c5a5be0 from the 2026-09-16 rollout.
